newsitem.title: USA: US stock index futures rally, end strongly higher.
newsitem.headline: US stock index futures rally, end strongly higher.

text.p: U.S. stock index futures rallied and ended higher, taking a bullish cue from a dramatic reversal in U.S. Treasury bonds, traders said.
U.S. March Standard and Poor's 500 futures surged to a fresh all-time high at 789.30, surpassing Monday's 784.60 record.
Traders said buy-stops helped the move, and said technical strength fed on itself after it became clear March S&Ps would not revisit their earlier session lows.
"It certainly was another record and it certainly was active," an S&P 500 futures trader said.
A dearth of surprises in Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan's testimony to the Senate Banking Committee heartened traders who had feared a market upset.
Greenspan's remarks painted an upbeat picture of the economy, although he did warn of some risks to wage-driven inflation.
He called the U.S. stock market's rise "breathtaking."
"It was such a good pop," one S&P 500 futures trader said. "It was all bonds and Greenspan, and there was some good buying on the rally," he said.
He said strength late in the day stemmed from expectations for favorable IBM earnings.
Later, IBM reported fourth-quarter earnings rose to $3.93 from $3.09, beating most analysts' estimates.

At settlement, March S&Ps were up 6.80 points to 786.95, KCBT Value Lines were up 1.20 at 708.40, NYSE Composites were up 2.75 at 413.80, Nikkeis were up 305 at 17,645 and Nasdaq 100s were up 11.90 at 919.50.
